# Compatibility

<!-- Generated by fixtures/tools/compat.py; edit only between the hand-written markers. -->

What surimono does and doesn't do yet, from test results. Every known failure is listed with the test that proves it. Expectations come from Chrome, specs and WPT, and are never edited to match surimono's output.

Results: fixtures from 99c363cd359c281c34bf99e6de0337f3bf569ac8 (surimono CLI surimono 0.0.0, sha256 7c8d26582fbe, commit 99c363cd359c281c34bf99e6de0337f3bf569ac8); hostile scripts from their results file; benchmark from bench/run.sh.

### Speed and memory against Grover

From `bench/run.sh` on GitHub Actions, commit 15b530e02, 20 runs; Chromium Google Chrome for Testing 153.0.8010.12, grover 1.2.10, fulgur 0.40.0. Medians; peak memory is summed PSS over the process tree. The full table is in `bench/results/15b530e0/summary.md`.

| System | Cold | Warm | Peak memory, cold | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Grover (Chrome) | 1,698 ms | 1,268 ms | 589 MB | measured |
| surimono + fulgur (Ruby) | 694 ms | 538 ms | 101 MB | measured |
| surimono + fulgur (Rust) | 570 ms | 538 ms | 74 MB | measured |
| fulgur only, Chrome's SVGs (reference point) | 245 ms | 118 ms | 68 MB | reference point, not surimono |
| Grover (chrome-headless-shell) | 1,284 ms | 1,009 ms | 383 MB | measured |
| Grover, new Chrome per document | — | 1,534 ms | — | measured |

Memory target (`docs/SPEC.md`): at least 5× lower peak (summed PSS) than Grover, set by Kay at checkpoint 2 (4 Nov 2026, down from 10×). Measured, cold: 5.8× Ruby and 8.0× Rust. fulgur alone, with no JavaScript, reaches 8.7×, which is why the target isn't higher: it is expected to bound surimono's ratio, not a proven bound. Against Grover on chrome-headless-shell, the leanest Chrome it can run: 3.8× Ruby and 5.2× Rust.

## Known gaps

| Gap | Evidence | Effect |
|---|---|---|

## Where the spec and Chromium disagree

Every row is a conflict the fleet rule settles: the spec wins for DOM behaviour, so surimono follows the spec and differs from Chromium 153.0.8010.12. None of them changes how a page prints. `wpt/probes` reruns each one in both. One more spec-against-Chromium conflict is settled the same way but can change what a page does, so it sits in Known gaps: `while (…) await sleep(0)`.

| Behaviour | Spec, and surimono | Chromium 153 | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `!important` in a `style` attribute: where a declaration stays | CSSOM keeps source order: `height: 1px; color: red !important; width: 1px` reads back unchanged | Sometimes moves it after the normal ones: `height: 1px; width: 1px; color: red !important;`, yet keeps `color: red !important; width: 1px;` | `crates/dom/src/style_attr.rs`, `important_keeps_source_order`; review of #97 |
| `style` attribute order in the serialized tag, when a script sets `element.style` and then another attribute | CSSOM §6.6 updates the attribute at once, so `style` comes first | Adds it lazily, when something reads the attributes, so it serializes last | `crates/dom/tests/real_world.rs`, `style_last`, which moves `style` to the end of each tag on both sides of the comparison (#104) |
| `normalize()` on a lone text node | DOM §4.4 step 4, "replace data" (§4.10 step 4): one `characterData` record, with the old value | No record | `crates/dom/tests/observers.rs`, `normalize_queues_its_records_in_tree_order`; review of #105 |
| `normalize()` merging several text nodes | One `characterData` record, then all the removals | One `characterData` and one removal per merged node, and an empty member of the run is removed before merging | Same test and review |
| `previousSibling` in the record of `a.replaceChild(p, q)`, where `p` was `q`'s previous sibling | §4.2.3 reads it before adopting, so the record has `p` | Null | Review of #105. Probed on main 89343c8f |
| `outerHTML` with text at the edge of the new content, beside a text node | DOM Parsing has no merge step: one record, adding the element and the text | Merges the text edge with the next text node: `add[B,"2z"]`, then a `characterData` and a removal | Review of #105. Probed on main 89343c8f |
| `splitText` record order | §4.11: insert first, then replace data | `characterData` first | Review of #105. Probed on main 89343c8f |
| `[a="b" s]`, the case-sensitive flag | Selectors 4 defines `s`, and it matches here | `SyntaxError` | `wpt/probes`, `selectors` |
| `HTMLDocument` | HTML §7.2.2: `window.HTMLDocument` is the `Document` interface object, so `HTMLDocument === Document`, and `document.constructor.name` is `Document` | A separate interface: `HTMLDocument === Document` is false, and the name is `HTMLDocument` | `wpt/probes`, `htmldoc`. `crates/dom/tests/nodes.rs` (#131). 20 subtests of `dom/events/passive-by-default.html` put that name in their own names, `… for HTMLDocument`, so ours report `… for Document` and they count as lost |
| `label.control` with `for`, on a label not in a document | HTML §4.10.4 looks "in the tree", so a detached label finds the control beside it or inside it, and `click()` reaches it | Null, and the click goes nowhere: it looks only in the document | `wpt/probes`, `label`. Review of #135; `a_labels_control_ignores_hidden_inputs_and_stays_in_its_tree` in `crates/dom/tests/events.rs` |
| A listener that throws: when the report comes | WebIDL "invoke a callback function" cleans up first, so the checkpoint comes before the report: `L1,m,E1,em,E2,L2` | Reports first: `L1,E1,E2,m,em,L2` | `wpt/probes`, `throwlistener`. Review of #149 |
| A function timer that throws: when the report comes | The same text: `T,m,E1,em,E2`. A string timer is a classic script, reported inside its run: `T,E1,E2,m,em`, as in Chromium | `T,E1,E2,m,em` for both | `wpt/probes`, `throwtimer`. #155 and its review |
| When `<svg onload>` fires | SVG 2 §15.2: once all the document's resources have loaded, so every `svg` in one step just before the window's `load`, in end-tag order | A nested `svg` fires as it closes, before `DOMContentLoaded`; an outermost one just before the window's `load`, in an order that isn't tree order | `wpt/probes`, `svgh`. `crates/dom/DESIGN.md`, "Events and the page's life"; review of #155 |
| `history.state` after a same-URL navigation | HTML: the new entry has no state, so `popstate`'s state and `history.state` are null | Keeps `history.state` | `crates/dom/DESIGN.md`, "Location and history"; #153 |
| A host that `url/IdnaTestV2`'s data has valid and Chromium refuses: 49 subtests, every one of the test that Chromium fails. 42 write ≮ or ≯ as `<` or `>` followed by U+0338, such as `ToASCII("≯1.。ß")` (3 of them also ≠ as `=` and U+0338); 7 hold the plane-3 code point U+3E8AC or U+3F8CD, such as `ToASCII("ⴍ𿣍ꡨ֮.ⴞ")` | UTS 46 as the test's data has it. Normalizing comes first, so `>` and U+0338 are ≯ (U+226F), which is valid: `new URL('https://>\u03381.x/x').host` is `xn--1-ogo.x`. The two code points are valid in ICU 2.4.0's IDNA data, through `url`'s `idna`: `new URL('https://ⴍ𿣍ꡨ֮.ⴞ/x').host` is `xn--5cb172r175fug38a.xn--mlj`. All 49 pass here | `TypeError: Invalid URL` for all 49. It takes the same host written with the one character ≯ or ≮ (`xn--1-ogo.x`), and `=` followed by U+0338 | `url/IdnaTestV2.any.html` in `wpt/results/wpt-results.json` and `wpt/baseline/chrome.json`, counted against the test's data; Chromium's answers for all 49 and for the composed forms asked of 153.0.8010.12 with `new URL`. The 42 passed on ICU 2.2.0 as well; the 7 pass since E3-R1 stage A moved ICU to 2.4.0 |
| `innerHTML` in an XML document with a prefix nothing binds: `svg.innerHTML = '<q:b/>'` | HTML, XML fragment parsing: an XML namespace well-formedness error throws a `SyntaxError`, and the element keeps its children | No exception: a `q:b` element in no namespace | `wpt/probes`, `xmlfragns`, its `unbound` line. Review of #190 |
| `XMLSerializer` on an attribute whose prefix an ancestor binds to another namespace | DOM Parsing keeps the prefix when "local prefixes map does not contain prefix", and that map holds only this element's declarations: `<child xmlns:p="uri2" p:foobar="v"/>`. **surimono doesn't follow it here**: it gives `ns1`, as WPT and Chromium do | `<child xmlns:ns1="uri2" ns1:foobar="v"/>`, which `domparsing/XMLSerializer-serializeToString.html` expects | `wpt/probes`, `xmlprefix`. `crates/dom/src/xml.rs` |

Probed on main 89343c8f: `false`, `defaultPrevented` true |

Probed on main a68123fb with one page in `render_page` and in Chromium 153.0.8010.12: the attribute reads `-1` here and `0` there, `value` 0 in both. The bar prints empty either way |

## Printing gaps in fulgur 0.40.0 seen by the fixtures

These are fulgur's (or Blitz's or parley's), not surimono's. Each is drafted for
upstream, with its cause and the smallest fix, under the id in the first column:
F in `docs/upstream/fulgur-layout-gaps-0.40.md`, B in `blitz-print-gaps-0.2.4.md`,
P in `parley-print-gaps-0.6.md`; fulgur 0.41.0 changes none of them (#176, #177).
The island fixture template avoids them, so page diffs measure the islands
(fixtures/README.md). The real-world pages don't: `fixtures/checkpoint-3` prints
each with surimono's printer-safe output (on by default since #180) and without it.
Printer-safe output writes three of these in a form fulgur 0.40.0 prints as Chrome
does (B1, F1, and B2 for a `<pre>`), only where Chrome prints the rewritten page
the same; the others need the printer. Each `fixtures/printers/reproducers/` page
named below scores fulgur 0.40.0 against Chrome on that gap alone
(`reproducers.md`). Repros were made with `fulgur render` and inspected in the PDF
content stream or its rasters.

| Gap | Repro | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| A single-side border ignores its colour and prints in `border-top-color`, so in `currentColor` unless the top colour is set (F1): `border-bottom: 1px solid #d0d7de` (or with `border-bottom-color`) prints black on black text; `border: 1px solid #d0d7de` on all sides prints the right colour | `<div style="border-bottom: 2px solid red; height: 10px">` strokes `0 0 0 RG`. `F1-border-side-colour.html`: 100.0% | Table row rules and header underlines print black instead of light grey. Printer-safe output adds the side's own colour as `border-top-color` in a sheet below the page's rules: `noscript-message` goes from 100.0% / 0.0% / 100.0% to a pass at 9.7% / 0.0% / 0.0% |
| A block-level `<svg>` (or `<img>`) ignores its `width` and `height` attributes and fills the content box (B1) | d3's charts: `<svg width="640" height="208">` under `svg { display: block }` fills the content box. `B1-block-svg-size.html`: 100.0% (colour 100.0%; hue 100.0%) | `d3-charts` fails at 100.0% / 100.0% / 100.0% without printer-safe output. With it, a sheet gives each such `<svg>` its attributes' size where no author declaration does: a pass at 0.0% |
| A forced break at the end of a block adds an empty line, as does the newline a `<pre>`'s text ends in (B2) | `<pre>one\ntwo\n</pre>` and `<div>one<br>two<br></div>` are three lines high; Chrome's are two. `B2-extra-line.html`: 16.9% (colour 100.0%) | Every Markdown code block (`<pre><code>…\n</code></pre>`) is a line taller. Printer-safe output leaves a `<pre>`'s last newline out; `marked-report` still fails for F2, F4 and F6 (67.5% / 84.8% / 100.0% with and without it) |
| A line that fits the page area in Chrome by under a pixel wraps: the content width is cut to whole pixels, 680 px for A4 with 15 mm margins where Chrome breaks against 680.3125 (F6, B6) | A filled block is 510.000 pt wide in fulgur's PDF where 180 mm is 510.236 pt. `F6-content-width.html`: 100.0% (colour 100.0%; hue 100.0%) | `marked-report`'s first paragraph ends its first line at "the print" instead of "the print guide", and everything below moves. Not rewritten: #180 doesn't ship the root-width rewrite, which prints the same in Chrome only under the conditions F6's draft lists |
| List markers sit against the text (F2) | Nested `<ul>` (disc, circle, square) and an `<ol>`: Chrome draws the bullets as shapes with a gap to the text; fulgur's touch it. `F2-list-markers.html`: 91.1% | `marked-report`'s lists. No rewrite keeps Chrome's print |

On `marked-report` the slanted words fall within the metric's tolerance; the difference is visible |

## Printing differences in Chrome seen by the fixtures

| Difference | Repro | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Chrome's PDF output drops `fill-opacity` on gradient fills | ECharts' area under a line (`areaStyle` with a linear gradient and its default opacity 0.7) is drawn as `<path fill="url(#zr1-g0)" fill-opacity="0.7">`. Chromium 153 applies the 0.7 on screen: a screenshot gives (240, 187, 153) at one point. Its printed PDF ignores it: (233, 159, 110) at the same point. fulgur prints (239, 187, 153), which agrees with the screen and with the SVG spec (`fill-opacity` applies to paint servers) | A semi-transparent gradient prints darker in Chrome's references than in fulgur or on screen. Spec and Chrome's own screen agree, so the fixtures avoid the case instead of taking a side: echarts-two-charts-latin sets the area's opacity to 1 |
| Chrome rounds `@page` sizes to 1/300 inch | An island page with `@page { size: 640px 340px }`: `pdfinfo` on Chrome's PDF gives 255.12 pt tall instead of 255 pt (380 px gives 285.12 pt). pdftoppm at 96 dpi then rasterises 341 rows where fulgur's exact 255 pt gives 340 | Page sizes differ by one row and the comparison fails on size alone. The fixtures use island sizes in multiples of 8 px (1/12 inch), which are exact; `gen-islands.mjs` refuses others |
| Chrome positions SVG text in 1/64 px layout units and rounds each advance to them | `crates/gfx/src/svg/text.rs` (P1-GFX-05), `layout_matches_chrome`: surimono's outlines use Parley's exact advances (equal to `measureText`'s to 0.0007 px), so each glyph lands up to 1/128 px per preceding character from Chrome's, at most 0.049 px on the reference strings | Far below the fixture comparison's 1 px tolerance; recorded so nobody chases it |
